label: AI Agent
description: An AI that can use tools (search, APIs, your code) on its own, step by step, until the task is done. It reads and writes the conversation (the `messages` field). Technical: LangChain create_agent.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model that does the thinking. Plug in an “AI model” block.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Things the agent may use, such as a web API or your own Python function. Plug in any number of tool blocks.

inputs.name: middleware
inputs.description: Optional. Add-ons that change how the agent behaves: limits, retries, safety checks. They run in the order you connect them.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the agent has finished: connect the next step, or Finish.

system_prompt.title: Instructions for the agent
system_prompt.description: Tell the AI who it is and how to behave, in plain words, e.g. “You are a friendly support assistant. Answer briefly.”

approve_tools.title: Tools that need approval
approve_tools.description: Pause for a human before these tools run (approve / edit / reject).

response_format.title: Structured output (JSON Schema)
response_format.description: When set, the agent's final answer is validated against this schema and written to the `structured_response` channel.

label: Agent from another framework
description: Runs an agent you built with another framework (OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, Agno, Strands, LlamaIndex, Microsoft Agent Framework, Claude Agent SDK) as one step. Point it at the agent in your Workspace. It is a black box on the canvas: one step, with its input and answer in the trace. Runs inside this server, so the hosted edition does not offer it.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the agent has answered: connect the next step, or Finish.

framework.title: Framework
framework.description: Which framework built the agent. Its package must be installed (exports add it).

import_path.title: Agent
import_path.description: Where the agent is in your Workspace, e.g. tools.agents:support_agent. A function with no arguments that returns the agent also works (a fresh agent per run).

prompt.title: What to send the agent
prompt.description: The agent's input. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}. Leave empty to send the latest chat message.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the agent's answer. Choose `messages` to add it to the chat.

approve.title: Ask a person before it runs
approve.description: Pause with an approval card showing what will be sent; a rejection skips the agent.

side_effects.title: Side effects
side_effects.description: What the agent's own tools can do, for the blast-radius view and dry runs.

label: Ask AI
description: Sends a question or instruction (the prompt) to an AI model and saves its reply. Use {{ state.<field> }} in the prompt to insert data from earlier steps.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model that writes the reply. Plug in an “AI model” block.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the reply is saved: connect the next step, or Finish.

prompt.title: Instructions for the AI (prompt)
prompt.description: What you want the AI to do. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}, e.g. Summarize this: {{ state.question }}

output.title: Save the reply in
output.description: The data field that receives the AI's answer. Add fields in the Inspector (click empty canvas).

label: Helper Agent
description: A specialist a Planning Agent can hand a task to (for example “researcher” or “reviewer”). Its name is how the Planning Agent asks for it, and its description says when to use it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional. The AI model this helper uses. Without one it uses the Planning Agent's model.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Tools only this helper may use.

inputs.name: middleware
inputs.description: Optional. Add-ons for this helper: limits, retries, safety checks.

outputs.name: subagent
outputs.description: Plug this into a Planning Agent's “subagents” input.

description.title: When to use it
description.description: Shown to the main agent to decide when to delegate.

system_prompt.title: Instructions for the agent
system_prompt.description: Tell the AI who it is and how to behave, in plain words, e.g. “You are a friendly support assistant. Answer briefly.”

approve_tools.title: Tools that need approval
approve_tools.description: Pause for a human before these tools run (approve / edit / reject).

label: Planning Agent
description: A stronger AI agent for big, multi-step jobs: it writes a plan, keeps notes in files, and can hand parts of the work to helper agents. It reads and writes the conversation (`messages`). Technical: deepagents create_deep_agent.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model that does the planning and thinking. Plug in an “AI model” block.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Things the agent may use, such as a web API or your own Python function.

inputs.name: middleware
inputs.description: Optional. Add-ons that change how the agent behaves: limits, retries, safety checks.

inputs.name: subagents
inputs.description: Optional. Helper agents it can hand tasks to. Plug in “Helper Agent” blocks.

inputs.name: backend
inputs.description: Optional. Where the agent keeps its notes and files. Without one, files last only for this run.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the agent has finished: connect the next step, or Finish.

system_prompt.title: Instructions for the agent
system_prompt.description: Tell the AI who it is and how to behave, in plain words, e.g. “You are a friendly support assistant. Answer briefly.”

approve_tools.title: Tools that need approval
approve_tools.description: Pause before these tools run; built-ins such as write_file or task are allowed.

response_format.title: Structured output (JSON Schema)
response_format.description: When set, the agent's final answer is validated against this schema and written to the `structured_response` channel.

label: Remote agent (A2A)
description: Asks an agent running elsewhere over the Agent2Agent protocol (A2A), whatever framework it uses. Paste its Agent Card address. When the remote agent needs more information, the run pauses and asks a person.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the agent has answered: connect the next step, or Finish.

url.title: Agent address
url.description: The Agent Card URL (…/.well-known/agent-card.json) or the agent's A2A endpoint.

prompt.title: What to send the agent
prompt.description: The agent's input. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}. Leave empty to send the latest chat message.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the agent's answer. Choose `messages` to add it to the chat.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Sent with every request, e.g. Authorization. Use a secret for keys.

approve.title: Ask a person before it runs
approve.description: Pause with an approval card showing what will be sent; a rejection skips the agent.

allow_private_network.title: Allow private network
allow_private_network.description: Allow addresses on a private or local network (an agent inside your company). Off: such addresses are refused.

label: Remote agent (MCP)
description: Calls one tool of an MCP server as a step, for example an agent published as an MCP tool. Plug an “App connector (MCP)” block into its tools input and name the tool.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: The MCP server (App connector) whose tool this step calls.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the agent has answered: connect the next step, or Finish.

tool.title: Tool
tool.description: The tool's name, as “Browse tools” on the connector lists it.

arguments.title: Arguments
arguments.description: The tool's arguments; each value may insert data with {{ state.<field> }}.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the agent's answer. Choose `messages` to add it to the chat.

approve.title: Ask a person before it runs
approve.description: Pause with an approval card showing what will be sent; a rejection skips the agent.

label: AI model
description: The AI “brain” (Claude, GPT, Gemini, a local model…) that AI steps use to think and write. One model block can power several steps. Can fall back to backup models and reuse answers to repeated requests. Technical: init_chat_model("provider:model").

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Plug this into the “model” input of an Ask AI step, an agent, or an add-on that needs a model.

model.title: Model
model.description: provider:model, e.g. anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5, openai:gpt-5.5, ollama:llama3.3, lmstudio:<model>

base_url.title: Base URL
base_url.description: The provider's server address; for local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) only when not on the default port

api_key.title: API key (secret reference)
api_key.description: A project secret holding the key. Empty: the project secret or server variable named after the provider (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY)

fallbacks.title: Backup models
fallbacks.description: If this model fails (the service is down, out of quota, too slow), the same request goes to these models in order. Each uses its provider's own key (the project secret or server variable named after the provider) and this block's temperature, output limit and timeout.

cache_ttl.title: Reuse answers for (s)
cache_ttl.description: Answer an identical request (same messages, tools and settings) from the cache for this many seconds, without calling the provider and at no cost. Empty: never reuse answers. Best for steps whose answer should not change, such as classifying or extracting.

label: Backup models
description: If the agent's AI model fails (for example the service is down), tries these backup models in order. Technical: ModelFallbackMiddleware.

inputs.name: models
inputs.description: The backup AI models, tried first to last. Plug in one or more “AI model” blocks.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: Limit AI calls
description: Stops the agent after a set number of AI model calls, so it cannot loop forever or run up a big bill. Technical: ModelCallLimitMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: Limit tool use
description: Limits how many times the agent may use its tools (all of them, or one), per run or per conversation. Technical: ToolCallLimitMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: Pick tools first
description: When an agent has many tools, a (cheaper) AI model first picks the few that matter for each request. Technical: LLMToolSelectorMiddleware.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional. The AI model that picks the tools. Without one the agent's own model does it.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: Protect personal data
description: Finds personal data (emails, card numbers and so on) in the conversation and blocks, hides or masks it. Technical: PIIMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

detector.title: Custom detector (regex)
detector.description: Optional regular expression that replaces the built-in detector.

label: Quality check
description: Before the agent answers, a second AI checks the work against your checklist and sends it back with what is missing, up to a set number of times. Technical: deepagents RubricMiddleware; grading streams as ac.rubric events.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model that checks the work. Plug in an “AI model” block.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Tools the checker may use to verify the work (run tests, read files).

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.description: What done looks like, one criterion per line

grader_instructions.title: Grader instructions
grader_instructions.description: Replaces the grader's default system prompt

label: Retry AI calls
description: Tries a failed AI model call again, waiting a little longer each time. Technical: ModelRetryMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

on_failure.title: When retries are exhausted
on_failure.description: continue = return an error message to the model; error = raise

label: Retry tools
description: Tries a failed tool again, waiting a little longer each time. Technical: ToolRetryMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

on_failure.title: When retries are exhausted
on_failure.description: continue = return an error message to the model; error = raise

label: Shorten long chats
description: When the conversation gets too long, replaces old messages with a short summary so the AI keeps working. Technical: SummarizationMiddleware.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model that writes the summary. Plug in an “AI model” block.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: To-do list
description: Gives the agent a to-do list it can write, so it plans multi-step work before doing it. Technical: TodoListMiddleware.

outputs.name: middleware
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “middleware” input.

label: Agent task
description: One CrewAI agent (a role, a goal, a backstory) does one task and saves its answer in a field. Only in workflows designed for CrewAI. A guardrail is a rule in plain words that the answer must follow: the model checks each answer against it and the agent tries again when it does not (up to the number of tries). Use {{ state.<field> }} in the texts. Technical: a CrewAI Task with an LLM guardrail, run by a one-agent Crew.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model the agent (and the guardrail check) uses. Plug in an “AI model” block.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Tools the agent may use.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the task is done: connect the next step, or Finish.

role.title: Role
role.description: What the agent is, e.g. Support specialist.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: What the agent tries to achieve.

backstory.title: Backstory
backstory.description: Optional. Background that shapes how the agent works.

description.title: Task
description.description: What to do. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}, e.g. Answer this ticket: {{ state.ticket }}

expected_output.title: Expected answer
expected_output.description: What a good answer looks like, e.g. A reply of at most three sentences.

guardrail.title: Guardrail
guardrail.description: Optional. A rule the answer must follow, e.g. Never promise a refund. Checked by the model; a failing answer is redone.

guardrail_max_retries.title: Tries after a failed check
guardrail_max_retries.description: How many times the agent may redo an answer the guardrail rejects; then the step fails.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the agent's answer.

label: Crew
description: A CrewAI team of agents, each with a role, a goal and a backstory, works through a list of tasks. Only in workflows designed for CrewAI. The tasks run one after another (each sees the earlier answers), or a manager hands them out. The last task's answer is saved in a field. Use {{ state.<field> }} in goals, backstories and tasks. Technical: a CrewAI Crew run with kickoff_async.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The AI model every agent of the crew (and the manager) uses. Plug in an “AI model” block.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Optional. Tools every agent of the crew may use.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go when the crew has finished: connect the next step, or Finish.

name.title: Name
name.description: A short name the tasks use to pick this agent, e.g. researcher.

role.title: Role
role.description: What the agent is, e.g. Senior research analyst.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: What the agent tries to achieve.

backstory.title: Backstory
backstory.description: Optional. Background that shapes how the agent works.

default.name: researcher
default.goal: Find the key facts about {{ state.topic }}

default.name: writer
default.goal: Turn the facts into a short, clear report

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: The work, in order. Each task's answer is passed to the next one.

description.title: Task
description.description: What to do. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}.

expected_output.title: Expected answer
expected_output.description: What a good answer looks like, e.g. A bullet list of five findings.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: The name of the agent that does it. Leave empty for the first agent (or, with a manager, for whoever the manager picks).

default.description: List the five most important facts about {{ state.topic }}
Write a short report from the facts

process.title: How the crew works
process.description: sequential: the tasks run in order, each by its agent. hierarchical: a manager (using the same model) hands out the tasks and checks the answers.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the last task's answer.

label: Run Python code
description: Runs a Python function you wrote in the Workspace. It receives the current data and returns the fields to update: `def run(state) -> dict`.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the code has run: connect the next step, or Finish.

label: Set values
description: Fills data fields with text you write, for example summary = “Ticket: {{ state.ticket }}”. Handy for preparing text before an AI step.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the values are set: connect the next step, or Finish.

label: Choose a path
description: Sends the workflow down different paths depending on the data, like “if the ticket is urgent go here, otherwise go there”. The first rule that matches wins; if none match it takes the default path.

cases.title: Rules

when.title: Condition
when.description: When this is true, take this path. Example: state.priority == "high" (CEL expression).

route.title: Path name
route.description: A short name in lowercase, e.g. urgent. It appears as an output on the block.

cases.description: Checked top to bottom; the first rule whose condition is true picks the path.

label: Group of steps
description: A small workflow inside one block, with its own data. Chosen fields are copied in before it runs and copied back out after. Double-click it to look inside.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the group has finished: connect the next step, or Finish.

workflow.title: Steps
workflow.description: The embedded workflow (double-click the node to open it)

label: Repeat for each item
description: Takes a list and runs one step once for every item, all at the same time. Each result must go into a list field (one that adds items).

outputs.name: each
outputs.description: Connect the step to run once per item.

outputs.name: empty
outputs.description: Where to go when the list is empty (if not connected: Finish).

items.title: List to go through
items.description: The data field holding the list, e.g. tickets.

item.title: Put the current item in
item.description: The data field the repeated step reads the current item from.

label: Wait for all
description: Waits until every branch connected into it has finished, then continues. Use it to bring parallel branches back together.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go once every branch has arrived: connect the next step, or Finish.

label: Search knowledge
description: Finds the passages of a knowledge base (documents you uploaded on the Knowledge page) that best answer a question, and saves them in a data field, each with its title, page and a citation number to quote.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the search: connect the next step (usually an AI step that answers from the passages), or Finish.

knowledge_base.title: Knowledge base
knowledge_base.description: The name of a knowledge base in this project (Knowledge page). Exports ship it as knowledge/<name>.jsonl.

query.title: Search for
query.description: Jinja template: the question to look up.

mode.title: Match by
mode.description: hybrid = words and meaning together (best in most cases); semantic = meaning (embeddings); keyword = exact words (BM25)

min_score.title: Minimum score
min_score.description: Drop passages scoring below this (0 = keep the best ones whatever their score)

output.title: Save the passages in
output.description: A list of {cite, title, text, page, source, score}; an AI step can quote them by [cite]

sources_output.title: Save the sources in
sources_output.description: Optional: the citation list ({cite, title, source, page}) to show under an answer

label: Forget memory
description: Deletes one saved memory by its key (name).

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the memory is deleted: connect the next step, or Finish.

space.title: Memory space
space.description: Same space + scope = same memories (a Deep Agent's long-term folder uses them too)

scope.title: Shared per
scope.description: user = the run's authenticated user (needs a context field with source 'user')

label: Look up memory
description: Searches what the workflow remembered in earlier runs and saves the matches (a list) into a data field.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the search: connect the next step, or Finish.

space.title: Memory space
space.description: Same space + scope = same memories (a Deep Agent's long-term folder uses them too)

scope.title: Shared per
scope.description: user = the run's authenticated user (needs a context field with source 'user')

query.title: Search for
query.description: Jinja template; empty = the most recent memories. Without a semantic index, words are matched.

label: Save to memory
description: Saves a value so later runs can find it again (long-term memory), under a key (name) you choose.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after saving: connect the next step, or Finish.

space.title: Memory space
space.description: Same space + scope = same memories (a Deep Agent's long-term folder uses them too)

scope.title: Shared per
scope.description: user = the run's authenticated user (needs a context field with source 'user')

value.title: Value to save
value.description: The data field whose value is remembered.

label: Saved files folder
description: A folder where a Planning Agent's files are kept after the run ends, shared across runs for a user, the workflow or one conversation. Technical: StoreBackend.

outputs.name: backend
outputs.description: Plug this into a Planning Agent's “backend” input.

mount.title: Folder
mount.description: Paths under this folder are stored long-term, e.g. /memories/

scope.title: Shared per
scope.description: user = the run's authenticated user (needs a context field with source 'user')

label: Scratch files
description: A scratch space for a Planning Agent's files that lasts only for this run and conversation. Technical: StateBackend.

outputs.name: backend
outputs.description: Plug this into a Planning Agent's “backend” input.

label: Ask a person
description: Pauses the workflow and asks a person a question (or shows a form). Their answer is saved in a data field and the workflow continues.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go once the person has answered: connect the next step, or Finish.

prompt.title: Question for the person
prompt.description: Jinja template, e.g. Which plan should we use for {{ state.customer }}?

response_schema.title: Answer form (JSON Schema)
response_schema.description: Optional; the answer is validated against it and the question is asked again if invalid.

output.title: Save the answer in
output.description: The data field that receives the person's answer.

label: Ask for approval
description: Pauses the workflow until a person approves or rejects (they can also edit the value shown). Put it before anything risky, like sending an email.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go once the person has decided: connect the next step, or Finish.

show.title: What the person reviews
show.description: The data field shown to the person (they may edit it).

output.title: Save the decision in
output.description: A data field that gets true (approved) or false (rejected).

label: Check for harmful content
description: Rates text for harmful content (violence, hate, harassment, self-harm, sexual, illegal activities) and flags it or stops the run. Plug in an AI model for real judgement; without one it uses a fixed list of phrases.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional but recommended: the AI model that rates the text. Without one, a fixed list of phrases is used.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the check: connect the next step, or Finish.

input.title: Text to check
input.description: The data field to check. For the conversation (messages) the newest message is checked.

on_fail.title: When it fails
on_fail.description: stop = end the run with an error that says why; flag = carry on and save the verdict for a later step to branch on.

flag_output.title: Save yes/no in
flag_output.description: Optional: a true/false field that is true when the check fails. Branch on it with Choose a path, e.g. state.flagged == true.

report_output.title: Save the details in
report_output.description: Optional: a field that receives what was found and why (never the personal data itself).

categories.title: Categories to block
categories.description: violence, hate, harassment, self_harm, sexual, illegal (illegal activities).

threshold.title: Sensitivity threshold
threshold.description: A category fails the check when its score (0 to 1) reaches this.

label: Check for prompt injection
description: Checks text for prompt injection: attempts to override the AI's instructions, fake system messages, hidden or encoded instructions, and requests for secrets. Uses fixed checks; plug in an AI model to also ask it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional: an AI model that also judges the text. The check fails when either the fixed checks or the model flag it.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the check: connect the next step, or Finish.

input.title: Text to check
input.description: The data field to check. For the conversation (messages) the newest message is checked.

on_fail.title: When it fails
on_fail.description: stop = end the run with an error that says why; flag = carry on and save the verdict for a later step to branch on.

flag_output.title: Save yes/no in
flag_output.description: Optional: a true/false field that is true when the check fails. Branch on it with Choose a path, e.g. state.flagged == true.

report_output.title: Save the details in
report_output.description: Optional: a field that receives what was found and why (never the personal data itself).

threshold.title: Sensitivity threshold
threshold.description: The check fails when the risk score (0 to 1) reaches this. Lower catches more but has more false alarms.

label: Check the output format
description: Checks that a data field (or the newest message) is JSON matching the format you describe, e.g. an AI reply that must have a summary and a priority. Can ask an AI model to fix it once.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional: the AI model that fixes invalid data when “Let the AI fix it once” is on.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the check: connect the next step, or Finish.

input.title: Text to check
input.description: The data field to check. For the conversation (messages) the newest message is checked.

on_fail.title: When it fails
on_fail.description: stop = end the run with an error that says why; flag = carry on and save the verdict for a later step to branch on.

flag_output.title: Save yes/no in
flag_output.description: Optional: a true/false field that is true when the check fails. Branch on it with Choose a path, e.g. state.flagged == true.

report_output.title: Save the details in
report_output.description: Optional: a field that receives what was found and why (never the personal data itself).

schema.title: Expected format (JSON Schema)
schema.description: The shape the data must have, e.g. an object with a required string field summary.

repair.title: Let the AI fix it once
repair.description: When the data does not match, ask the plugged-in AI model to correct it once before failing.

output.title: Save the checked data in
output.description: Optional: a field that receives the parsed JSON data when it is valid.

label: Hide personal data
description: Finds personal data (emails, phone and card numbers, IBANs, IP addresses, US social security numbers, your own patterns) in a data field and hides it, flags it or stops the run. Lists what kinds it found, never the values.

outputs.name: next
outputs.description: Where to go after the check: connect the next step, or Finish.

input.title: Text to check
input.description: The data field to check. For the conversation (messages) the newest message is checked.

on_fail.title: When it fails
on_fail.description: redact = hide what was found and carry on; flag = change nothing and save the verdict; stop = end the run with an error.

flag_output.title: Save yes/no in
flag_output.description: Optional: a true/false field that is true when the check fails. Branch on it with Choose a path, e.g. state.flagged == true.

report_output.title: Save the details in
report_output.description: Optional: a field that receives what was found and why (never the personal data itself).

types.title: What to look for
types.description: email, phone, credit_card (checked with the Luhn test), iban, ip_address, us_ssn.

custom_patterns.title: Your own patterns
custom_patterns.description: Optional regular expressions for your own kinds of personal data, e.g. AB-\d{6} for order ids.

strategy.title: How to hide it
strategy.description: redact = [REDACTED_EMAIL]; mask = keep the last 4 characters (****-1111); hash = a short fingerprint, the same for the same value.

output.title: Save the cleaned text in
output.description: Optional: leave empty to clean the field in place (the message itself, for messages).

label: App connector (MCP)
description: Connects an agent to all the tools of an app through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Use “Browse tools” to pick tools and see which ones change things.

outputs.name: tools
outputs.description: Every tool you picked from the app. Plug this into an agent's “tools” input.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: stdio starts a local process: local edition + admin setting only (E042)

env.title: Environment variables (stdio)
env.description: For the server process, e.g. its API key; a value can be a secret

tool_filter.title: Only these tools
tool_filter.description: Empty = every tool the server offers

discovered.title: Discovered tools
discovered.description: Filled by Browse tools; used to check approvals (W002, E033)

label: Memory tools
description: Lets an agent search and save its own memories (search_memory and save_memory tools) in one memory space.

outputs.name: tools
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “tools” input.

space.title: Memory space
space.description: Same space + scope = same memories (a Deep Agent's long-term folder uses them too)

scope.title: Shared per
scope.description: user = the run's authenticated user (needs a context field with source 'user')

label: Python tool
description: A Python function from the Workspace that an agent can use as a tool (a LangChain @tool).

outputs.name: tool
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “tools” input.

label: Web API tool
description: Lets an agent call a web service (an HTTP API), for example to look up an order. Its name is the tool name the AI sees; the URL can use the tool's inputs, e.g. https://api.example.com/orders/{{ args.order_id }}.

outputs.name: tool
outputs.description: Plug this into an agent's “tools” input.

description.title: What it does (shown to the model)

args_schema.title: Arguments (JSON Schema)
args_schema.description: What the model must provide; used in the URL as {{ args.<name> }}

send_args.title: Send arguments as
send_args.description: auto = none for GET/DELETE, JSON body otherwise

allowed_domains.title: Allowed domains
allowed_domains.description: Requests to any other host are refused (subdomains are allowed)

allow_private_network.title: Allow private network
allow_private_network.description: Let the allowed domains resolve to private, loopback or link-local addresses (internal services). Off: such hosts are refused, which also protects cloud metadata endpoints
